title: Top cohomology of an m-pseudo-coherent site complex is finite type
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a site with a sheaf of commutative rings and use its unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restrictions to an object mean restrictions to the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. A strictly perfect complex is a bounded cochain complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O$-modules. For $a\in\mathbf Z$, call $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ $a$-pseudo-coherent if locally on each site object there is a strictly perfect $P$ and a morphism $P\to K$ inducing cohomology isomorphisms in degrees $>a$ and a surjection in degree $a$. Let $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ be $m$-pseudo-coherent with $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i>m$. Then $H^m(K)$ is of finite type: on a covering of every site object it admits a surjection from a finite free structure module. No coherence condition on $\mathcal O$ is imposed.

proof.text: Fix an object $U$. By the stated definition of $m$-pseudo-coherence choose a covering $U_i\to U$ and strictly perfect approximations $P_i\to K|_{U_i}$. Restriction to a slice is exact [lem-sf-site-perfect-restriction-exact]: it preserves kernels, images and their quotients, hence $H^r(K|_{U_i})=H^r(K)|_{U_i}$ by the cohomology formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently $H^r(P_i)=0$ for $r>m$, and $H^m(P_i)\to H^m(K)|_{U_i}$ is an epimorphism. Restricting a finite-free splitting restricts both its maps and their identity equation; thus every further restriction of $P_i$ remains strictly perfect.

On the ringed slice $\mathcal C/U_i$, regard $P_i$ as a derived object. It is site-perfect: its bounded finite-free-retract complex itself supplies all the local models, using identity quasi-isomorphisms, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Apply [lem-sf-site-perfect-upper-model] with this object and $b=m$. Its vanishing hypothesis was verified in step 1. On a further covering $V_{ij}\to U_i$ it supplies a bounded strictly perfect complex $Q_{ij}$, zero in every degree $>m$, and an isomorphism in the derived category from $Q_{ij}$ to $P_i|_{V_{ij}}$. In particular their degree-$m$ cohomology sheaves are isomorphic. This application is to the perfect approximation, without requiring $K$ to be perfect.

Since $Q_{ij}^{m+1}=0$, the cohomology formula gives $H^m(Q_{ij})=\operatorname{coker}(d^{m-1}:Q_{ij}^{m-1}\to Q_{ij}^m)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Choose the defining splitting $Q_{ij}^m\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathcal O_{V_{ij}}^{\oplus N}\xrightarrow{p}Q_{ij}^m$, with $p\iota=1$. Compose $p$, the cokernel projection, the cohomology isomorphism of step 2, and the restriction to $V_{ij}$ of the epimorphism of step 1. Restriction from $\mathcal C/U_i$ to its slice at $V_{ij}$ is exact [lem-sf-site-perfect-restriction-exact], so it preserves epimorphisms and identifies $H^m(P_i|_{V_{ij}})$ with $H^m(P_i)|_{V_{ij}}$, as in step 1. This is an epimorphism $\mathcal O_{V_{ij}}^{\oplus N}\to H^m(K)|_{V_{ij}}$: the first map is split epic, the second is a cokernel projection, and the remaining maps are isomorphic or epic. Cokernels here are sheaf cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Covering transitivity composes $V_{ij}\to U_i\to U$, and successive restrictions identify with restriction to $V_{ij}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This is the required finite-type cover for the arbitrary object $U$.
